Keep protagonists and river direction consistent. Frame every scene comfortably within panel, not across gutters. Full comic occupies the canvas, no header/footer/title. STORY: THE TWO BRIDGES. LEFT TOP: Rabbit courier Pip with a sealed letter meets Rook by a river split by a small island; near wooden bridge reaches island, distant unfinished stone bridge reaches opposite village. LEFT MIDDLE: Rook keeps a simple wooden gate at the near bridge closed, Pip waits, clearly visibly unfinished far bridge. LEFT BOTTOM: Rook and hedgehog mapmaker Moss cross safely by a small workboat carrying tools to repair last stone arch on far bridge. RIGHT TOP: Moss finishes the stone bridge and Rook walks across inspecting it carrying his brass lamp, sturdy complete bridge, island behind him. RIGHT MIDDLE: From far shore, Rook raises bright lantern as a signal, Pip opens near wooden gate and begins crossing near bridge. RIGHT BOTTOM: Pip arrives at far village via the TWO connected bridges, delivers letter to an otter traveler Tess; Rook and Moss smile by the completed route. Clear sequential story: check the far bridge before opening the near gate. Give visual emphasis to two distinct bridges and island.
